lines: Meet Lumo, a learning game where every lesson you finish lights a lantern on an island.
I'm Wisp, your guide. Everything you're about to see is the real app, and this video was made by Lumo's own video pipeline.
Here's the problem. Most of what we learn is forgotten within a few weeks.
In Lumo, forgetting has a face. It's Gloom, the fog of forgetting, and your job is to keep it away.
Anyone can try an island before signing up.
A visitor picks an island,
watches its first short lesson,
and answers real questions. The server grades every answer, so the answer key never reaches the browser.
Signing up starts a short chat with me. I ask what you'd like to learn, and how much time you have each day.
You even choose my personality: gentle, cheerful, or a little cheeky.
Then, the map. Every stone is a lesson, and each island has its own guardian. Byte looks after Code Reef.
Lessons are short animated videos. Lumo writes the script, voices it locally, adds captions, and renders the animation itself.
Quick checks come next. Pick a wrong answer, and I explain that exact mistake, not just the right answer.
Get it right, and the lantern lights. You earn Light, and a daily flame keeps you coming back.
And here's the heart of Lumo. The next day, as you start to forget, the fog creeps back over the map.
A spaced repetition model called FSRS works out when each idea is fading, and a two minute review clears the fog.
Miss a few days, and there's no guilt trip. Lumo welcomes you back, and your best flame is kept forever.
Finish an island and claim a certificate. Anyone can verify it with its public link.
Instructors build islands in the studio, unit by unit.
Or they can ask me to draft a whole unit from just a topic.
I write the lesson and its questions, run the code in a sandbox to check every answer, and render the video.
But nothing reaches learners until a person has checked every question. The unit stays hidden until it's published.
Learners can report any question. Admins see exactly what the learner was shown, and every decision is logged.
Admins also review courses before they go live, and decide who can teach.
Under the hood, the database makes every decision. Row level security guards every table, and grading happens inside Postgres.
A hundred and sixty three automated tests keep it honest. And it costs nothing to run: free tiers only, with the voice and the video made on one laptop.
That's Lumo. Learn it once, and keep it for good.
